description: Machine-readable registry of AiXia AI access levels for QA, council review, and future MCP tool planning. Aligns with qa-agent/ai-access-boundary.md and qa-agent/ai-function-access-map.md.

levels.name: No AI access
levels.definition: Function or data must not be accessed or influenced by any AI assistant or tool.
exampleFunctions: Owner-only secret configuration stores
Raw security keys or token surfaces if ever exposed in UI by mistake
restrictions: No model or tool may read, summarize, or navigate this surface.

levels.name: Explain only
levels.definition: AI may describe what a page or concept means using only information already visible to the user.
exampleFunctions: Page explanation
Field help text expansion
Clarifying UI labels for the current screen
restrictions: Must not fetch or infer hidden records beyond current manual access.

levels.name: Navigate only
levels.definition: AI may suggest navigation targets such as routes or tabs that the user is already allowed to open manually.
exampleFunctions: Deep link suggestions within allowed routes
Guided next-step navigation without executing workflows
restrictions: Must not open admin-only routes for non-admin users.

levels.name: Read and search allowed records
levels.definition: AI may query or summarize records that the user role may already read in the active tenant, including record-level checks.
exampleFunctions: Registry search assistance
Read-only finance or HR summaries for authorized roles
restrictions: Must enforce user role, tenant, and record-level permission checks equivalent to manual access.
Must not broaden search scope beyond manual permissions.

levels.name: Prepare draft
levels.definition: AI may assemble draft content or draft records that still require explicit user review before commit.
exampleFunctions: Draft expense or finance forms
Draft HR letters or employee communications where policy allows
Draft documents or PDFs from allowed fields only
restrictions: Drafts must be clearly labeled and previewed before save when policy requires.
Must not auto-submit official records without confirmation.

levels.name: Execute after confirmation
levels.definition: AI may perform mutating actions only after explicit user confirmation and successful permission checks.
exampleFunctions: Submit official records after confirmation
Archive or restore records after confirmation where role allows
Execute approved finance or HR workflow steps after confirmation
restrictions: Confirmation dialogs must be explicit and intentional.
Must never silently mutate production data.

levels.name: Execute automatically within limited safe rules
levels.definition: AI may auto-execute only narrowly scoped, reversible, user-configured actions that cannot violate tenant isolation or permissions.
exampleFunctions: User-enabled auto-sort of a personal task list within one tenant
Low-risk UI preference toggles explicitly opted in by the user
restrictions: Limited to safe, reversible, user-configured actions only.
Must remain disabled by default unless user explicitly opts in with clear scope.
Must not include archive, delete, payment, payroll, or cross-record writes.

levels.name: Owner AI only
levels.definition: Only Owner AI may access or act against these capabilities; used for platform-wide governance and owner-grade improvement prompts.
exampleFunctions: Owner system improvement prompt generation
Cross-tenant readiness diagnostics reserved to the platform owner
restrictions: Normal users and Personal User AI cannot access.
Must never be exposed in standard user-facing AI surfaces.

levels.name: Never expose to AI
levels.definition: Hard deny-list surfaces where no AI type may read, infer, navigate, or act, regardless of role.
exampleFunctions: Highly classified security material if ever rendered
Emergency legal hold buckets if introduced
restrictions: No AI type should access this function or data.
Must be excluded from MCP tool catalogs and from model context policies.
